transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess the main thing is work has been taking me longer than it should. I’m an electrician, and I keep finding myself going back over jobs—checking breakers, labels, torque marks, photos, that kind of thing. Sometimes I’ll even drive back to a site just to make sure I didn’t miss something.

I know being careful is part of the job, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but… simple installs are starting to take way longer, and I think people are noticing. That’s what made me think I should probably talk to someone.
Do you feel like you have to check these things, even if you know they’re already correct, or is it more of a choice?

Yeah… I mean, I’d like to say it’s a choice, because I know the work is probably correct the first time. But it doesn’t really feel optional in the moment.

I’ll check the breaker, the label, the torque mark, the photo—then I’ll think, “Okay, that’s fine,” and a few minutes later I’m back looking at it again. Sometimes I even end up driving back to a site just to be sure. I know that probably sounds excessive, but it’s like I can’t settle until I’ve gone over it enough, and then a simple install takes way longer than it should. People are starting to notice, which is embarrassing.

When you’re checking the breakers, labels, or other things, do you have specific thoughts that come up—like a fear that something bad might happen if you don’t check, or thoughts that won’t go away until you do?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, because obviously I do know what I’m doing. But the thought that keeps coming up is, like, what if I missed one loose neutral, or left something in a panel or disconnect that could heat up and start a fire.

Even after I’ve checked it, that thought sort of barges back in. I’ll try to tell myself, “No, you already looked at it,” but it doesn’t really drop. Sometimes it follows me the whole way home, and then I’m thinking about whether I should go back and make sure. Does that make sense?
Do these checking behaviors happen almost every time you do a job, or are there times when you feel you can skip them without that anxious thought coming up?

It’s… it’s most jobs now, honestly. I don’t know if I’d say every single time, but it happens enough that it feels like part of the job now, even though I know it shouldn’t.

I’ll tell myself, “You checked the breaker, you checked the label, you’ve got the photo, it’s fine,” but then I end up going back over it again anyway. Sometimes it’s just one more look, and sometimes it turns into checking the torque marks and photos again, or even driving back to the site if I can’t let it go.

I can skip it once in a while if it’s really straightforward, but a lot of the time that anxious thought shows up, and then I feel like I need to check until it feels settled. That’s why things that should be simple are taking way longer than they should. I know that probably sounds like overdoing it.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms of recurrent intrusive thoughts related to potential harm (e.g., fire due to an electrical error) and repetitive checking behaviors (e.g., rechecking breakers, labels, torque marks, driving back to job sites) that cause significant distress and impairment in functioning are most consistent with obsessive-compulsive disorder (F42.9). Other candidates (F43.2, F40.2, F32.9) are less likely given the specific nature of the symptoms and the presence of both obsessions and compulsions.
